title: How a few still pictures become an animation
notes: The six-scene pilot brief from docs/YOUTUBE_PIPELINE.md as an executable manifest for tools/production.py (docs/PRODUCTION.md). Input paths are this machine's; point them at your own music and fonts. Every beat type of the pixel-stage template appears once or more.

scenes.title: One picture holds still
scenes.script: A tiny character stands still. Now its feet move, its body rises, and it seems to hop. The illusion begins with a small collection of carefully chosen pictures.

scenes.title: Choose the important poses
scenes.script: Each picture is a frame. For a hop, we can draw a crouch, a push, a floating pose, and a landing. These poses explain the action before we add detail.

scenes.title: Put the pictures in order
scenes.script: Play those frames in order and the character begins to move. Change the order, and the same pictures tell a different story. A clear sequence makes the movement easy to follow.

scenes.title: Timing gives the action weight
scenes.script: How long we hold each pose matters too. A brief push followed by a longer pause in the air feels different from evenly spaced poses. Timing helps an action feel light or heavy.

scenes.title: Revise one part
scenes.script: Because the pictures stay editable, we can change a color or improve a pose without starting again. Then we watch the sequence to check that the correction helps the whole movement.

scenes.title: Watch and listen together
scenes.script: Finally, we combine the animation with narration and captions. We watch, listen, and make another small revision. Simple pictures, deliberate timing, and careful review bring the character to life.
